Synopsis:
    US equity futures opened September under pressure, with Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq E-minis all declining (down 0.4%, 0.47%, and 0.9% respectively). The selloff is driven by elevated Treasury yields, rising oil prices, heightened rate-hike expectations, and Middle East tensions. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has reinforced inflation as the central bank's primary mandate. Key near-term catalysts include the JOLTS report and Friday's nonfarm payrolls. Chip stocks lead declines; energy names outperform. Seasonal headwinds add to the bearish backdrop, though some strategists urge staying invested.
